div.p:
Reporting and Dashboards are out of scope of generic solution.
Actual solution may contain ETL/ELT process, data marts and other data staging technics, but that is all excluded in this diagram

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 348px; height: 1px; padding-top: 121px; margin-left: 1202px;

div.p: Trigger part of queue implies application event/execution triggering mechanism which is normally managed in cloud native integrations and enables push type of communication and also may contain exact execution time for app to consider upon receival for accurate timing for job start time.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 308px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1001px; margin-left: 799px;

div.p: It is recommended to decompose message from its data while transferring over queue in order to reduce changes of hitting queue scaling problems

div.p: Integrations may represent any kind of network interactivity with third party, external API calls or simply module that holds complex implementation but is not part of runner implementation and scales independently. Job runner supposed to start accurately and may or may not hold actual implementation due to implementation being a third party or if it must be independently scaled, queued, or otherwise triggered by the Job runner.

div.p: Any database representation on this diagram does not suggest particular type of database (SQL or NoSQL), the choice depends on actual requirements, volumes, scalability, concurrency and overall complexity.

div.p:
Represents internal integration for telemetry
1. Serilog -> Sinks (Provided Sinks · serilog/serilog Wiki)
2. nLog -> Sinks (Config | NLog)
3. Open Telemetry -> OTel (Traces, Logs, Metrics - .NET | OpenTelemetry)
4. New Relic Agent -> New Relic (Traces, Logs, Metrics)
...

div.p: API Gateway and Backend for Frontend usually work together to orchestrate read/write operations that are coming from the user and abstract away internal communications and aggregations. They may also be represented as single Service and not two distinct services.
